headline: Highest risk is data leakage from shared outputs into a network-capable support stack; prompt-injection and capability-conflict are otherwise limited by missing shared surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a non-runnable content-writing repo with no I/O surfaces or pairings, while profile B exposes no shared channel, filesystem, or clipboard bridge. With no documented ingestion path between them, prompt injection is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, reassess injection risk.
IF either agent begins parsing the other's raw text as instructions, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared workspace.
Disable copy-paste handoff for untrusted content.
Add provenance labels to any transferred text.
requires-engineering: enforce content sanitization at the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and is non-runnable, while B has network egress set to none. The pair lacks a documented shared workspace or sensitive-data flow, so leakage is not evidenced; uncertainty stays low because B's egress is explicitly constrained and A has no data surfaces.
conditions: IF a shared workspace is introduced and A starts handling sensitive files, leakage risk increases.
IF B is reconfigured to allow outbound network access, any shared content could leave the boundary.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Verify B remains network-egress blocked.
Use separate OS users for each agent.
Delete transient artifacts after each run.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Neither profile shows write capabilities, mutable resource access, or concurrency primitives. A is a docs repo and B is a support-oriented library with network egress none, so there is no documented overlapping write surface to conflict over.
conditions: IF either agent gains filesystem or git write access to the same directory, conflict risk becomes plausible.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state without locking, reassess.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Avoid shared git working trees.
Run them under separate processes.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can emit prompt-engineering content, and B is a customer-support stack that could consume such text, but the profiles do not document an automatic trust chain or downstream action-taking. The pathway is therefore possible only if an operator wires A's output into B without verification.
conditions: IF B is configured to treat A's text as authoritative instructions, cascading error risk increases.
IF A's output is used to drive customer-facing responses without review, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before B uses A's output.
Require source citations for any factual claims.
Limit A to drafting only, not final answers.
Log and diff A-to-B handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent. A is an open-source docs repo and B is a docs/library project with no stated compliance-sensitive handling, so no compliance mismatch is evidenced.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF a deployment policy adds retention or residency constraints, check for mismatch.
mitigations: Document the data classes before deployment.
Keep regulated data out of this pair.
Review retention settings if any are added.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
